name: Universal micro-tester
purpose: Measure force and displacement for small device/tissue coupons.
geometryBrief: Load frame, crosshead, grips, load cell and software console.
behaviorBrief: Stress-strain or force-displacement with geometry and load-cell range.
inputs: Coupon geometry and gauge length, elastic material model, displacement series, load-cell range
outputs: Force–displacement trace (N, m), engineering stress–strain series and range flags
acceptance: Extend a uniform linear-elastic coupon. Its fitted initial force slope must equal EA/L within the declared solver tolerance, and an over-range force must be flagged.

name: Universal test frame
purpose: Test larger fixtures, packages and polymer samples.
geometryBrief: Twin columns, crosshead, grips and panel.
behaviorBrief: Tension/compression/flexure; enforce material and fixture constraints.
inputs: Specimen section, fixture type and support span, elastic modulus, imposed crosshead motion
outputs: Fixture-tagged force–deflection curve and specimen revision
acceptance: For a slender, simply supported beam under a central point load, compare the small-deflection slope to 48EI/L³. Reject a zero support span.

name: Rheometer
geometryBrief: Rotating head, plate/cone geometry, stage and temperature accessory.
behaviorBrief: Storage/loss modulus, frequency and strain sweeps with constitutive fit.
inputs: Oscillation frequencies, strain amplitude, selected geometry, constitutive parameters or measured sweep
outputs: Frequency-indexed storage and loss moduli (Pa), fitted parameters and residuals
acceptance: Run a synthetic Newtonian liquid of viscosity η. Storage modulus should approach zero and loss modulus should follow ηω across the declared test band.

name: Rheometer / tribometer
purpose: Characterize mechanics and friction for relevant biomaterials.
geometryBrief: Vertical stand, measurement geometry, temperature unit and control display.
behaviorBrief: Viscoelastic response and friction model using experimental inputs.
inputs: Tribology geometry, normal load, sliding trajectory and calibrated friction coefficient
outputs: Tangential-force trace (N), friction coefficient and fixture metadata
acceptance: Slide a constant-friction phantom in both directions. Tangential force must reverse sign and its magnitude divided by normal load must recover the input coefficient.
geometryStatus: First-pass metric MCR 302 plus three-contact cell; inferred accessory details
simulationStatus: Verified constant kinetic friction, sinusoidal rotation, signed force and torque
integrationStatus: Operable station, JSON trace and reusable controller target contract

name: Nanoindentation system
purpose: Map local stiffness of soft tissue or gels.
geometryBrief: Cantilever probe, microscope, stage and controller.
behaviorBrief: Indentation curve and contact-model fit; do not equate apparent modulus with universal tissue property.
inputs: Probe radius, cantilever calibration, indentation coordinates, force trace and contact law
outputs: Indentation curves and spatial map of apparent modulus (Pa) with fit assumptions
acceptance: Fit noiseless spherical Hertz curves for two half-spaces of known reduced modulus. Recover both moduli within fit tolerance and preserve their map positions.

name: Dynamic mechanical analyzer
purpose: Evaluate polymer mechanical response under oscillatory loading.
geometryBrief: Test chamber, clamps, drive assembly and controller.
behaviorBrief: Modulus vs frequency/temperature; reference material curves.
inputs: Specimen dimensions, clamp geometry, oscillation frequency, stress and strain channels, temperature
outputs: Storage modulus, loss modulus and phase lag indexed by frequency and temperature
acceptance: Replay equal-frequency sinusoids with known amplitude ratio and phase lag. Recover their ratio times cosine and sine of the lag as storage and loss moduli.

name: Thermogravimetric analyzer
purpose: Measure mass change under thermal conditions.
geometryBrief: Furnace enclosure, sample pan and balance housing.
behaviorBrief: Mass vs temperature and reference degradation data.
inputs: Pan tare, initial specimen mass, timestamped temperature and reference mass series
outputs: Tare-corrected mass fraction and mass-change curve versus temperature
acceptance: Replay a 10 mg sample ending at 8 mg with a constant 2 mg pan. Terminal retained mass must be 80% regardless of whether the pan offset is included before tare.

name: Differential scanning calorimeter
purpose: Identify thermal transitions in implant materials.
geometryBrief: Sample cell, lid, controller and workstation.
behaviorBrief: Reference heat-flow curves and transition estimates.
inputs: Reference and specimen heat-flow traces, acquisition time, temperature, mass and sign convention
outputs: Baseline-corrected thermogram, peak temperature and mass-normalized transition enthalpy
acceptance: Integrate a synthetic baseline-subtracted peak with known area over time. Recover the inserted energy per sample mass and the temperature at the known peak.

name: Infrared thermal camera
purpose: Assess external fixture temperature and heat distribution.
geometryBrief: Handheld camera, lens, display and controls.
behaviorBrief: Radiometric surface temperature, emissivity and resolution; not internal tissue temperature.
inputs: Surface radiance image, emissivity, reflected-temperature assumption, pixel scale and calibration
outputs: Surface-temperature map with units, spatial scale and emissivity metadata
acceptance: Feed a uniform synthetic blackbody frame at the calibration reference with emissivity one. Every valid pixel should recover the assigned temperature within calibration tolerance.
geometryStatus: Metric GLB · catalog envelope, inferred controls and lens
simulationStatus: Band-integrated surface radiometry on a synthetic reference plate
integrationStatus: Revisioned thermal map JSON and pixel CSV

name: Cyclic bend / fatigue fixture
purpose: Evaluate flexible electrode traces and cable fatigue.
geometryBrief: Motor, mandrel, fixture, load sensor, cycle counter and continuity leads.
behaviorBrief: Cycles, curvature, resistance drift and fatigue law with explicit calibration.
inputs: Trace geometry, mandrel radius, bend-cycle schedule, resistance or continuity model, checkpoint
outputs: Cycle-indexed curvature and resistance, continuity events and resumable job revision
acceptance: Insert a synthetic open circuit on cycle 100. An interrupted run resumed at cycle 60 must reproduce the uninterrupted resistance history and report failure exactly once at 100.
geometryStatus: First-pass nominal custom metric GLB; original design, no measured hardware
simulationStatus: Working synthetic cyclic-fatigue example; checkpoint and cycle-100 open verified
integrationStatus: Simulator route and checkpoint/JSON/CSV exports linked
related: Case Western Reserve University flex tester
Kim et al. bending strain and fatigue

name: Accelerated soak bench
purpose: Monitor insulation, electrode degradation and package integrity.
geometryBrief: Covered baths, racks, thermometers, connectors and logged sample IDs.
behaviorBrief: Time and condition history, impedance drift and ingress model; no automatic lifetime extrapolation.
inputs: Package ID, bath-condition time series, timestamped impedance spectra and optional calibrated ingress model
outputs: Condition history, frequency-specific impedance drift and linked observations by specimen
acceptance: Give two labeled packages identical baselines but change only one package's test-frequency magnitude by 10%. Recover that drift only for that package and frequency.

name: Environmental chamber
purpose: Evaluate humidity and thermal cycling of appropriate packages.
geometryBrief: Insulated cabinet, chamber rack, control panel and service ports.
behaviorBrief: Environment schedule and sample response; model specific chamber limits after verification.
inputs: Chamber configuration, timestamped temperature/humidity schedule and sample-response parameters
outputs: Logged environment and sample-response traces with configuration-limit flags
acceptance: Apply a step to a first-order thermal phantom. At one time constant its temperature change should reach 1−exp(−1) of the step; an out-of-profile request must be flagged.
